description:
We are the Software & AI Team of RobEn Club, an engineering community founded in Cairo, Egypt, in 2013. For more than 13 years, RobEn has brought together students and young engineers who are passionate about robotics, artificial intelligence, software development, and creating technology that solves real-world problems.

(RobEn homepage, Software & AI team)
summary:
RedSight is a walk planner for astronauts exploring Mars on foot, built for one real place: the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp in Gale crater, where NASA’s Curiosity rover is driving today.

Mars maps are made for whole regions, but a crew of two leaving their habitat needs a plan for the next kilometre or two, and for the oxygen in their suits. A message to Earth takes up to 22 minutes each way, so the crew has to decide on the spot.

RedSight puts NASA orbital and rover data on one walk-scale map. The crew picks a science stop at a real Curiosity site and compares two modeled routes, the fastest and the one over the easiest ground, with walking time and oxygen for each astronaut. An oxygen slider shows where they would have to turn back, and a no-return line marks how far they can go and still get home. Mission Replay plays the walk with an oxygen gauge and drills such as a suit leak.

Every figure is a modeled estimate built from NASA sources, and each one is labelled Observed, Derived or Scenario.
